root_cause.text: The page reassignment loop in af_alg_pull_tsgl lacked a bounds check on the remaining page length (plen), allowing it to attempt reassigning a page even when no data remained to be processed, causing an off-by-one overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the condition `&& plen` to the existing `if (dst)` check before performing page reassignment. The commit message explicitly states "it may try to reassign one more page than necessary" when the original loop wasn't updated to account for the new page reassignment logic introduced in commit e870456d8e7c. Without this check, the loop would continue and attempt to reassign a page even after all necessary data had been processed (when plen becomes 0).

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability root cause describes an off-by-one overflow in af_alg_pull_tsgl where the page reassignment loop lacked a bounds check on the remaining page length (plen), allowing it to attempt reassigning a page even when no data remained. This commit FIXES the vulnerability by removing the complex dst_offset logic that was introduced in the problematic commit 72548b093ee3. The fix simplifies the code by: (1) removing the dst_offset parameter entirely from af_alg_pull_tsgl, (2) removing the conditional check 'if (dst_offset >= plen)' that was attempting to handle the offset case, and (3) directly reassigning pages without the offset complexity. The removed code block (lines with 'if (dst_offset >= plen)' and the associated offset handling) was the source of the bounds check issue. By reverting to out-of-place operation and eliminating the offset-based page reassignment logic, this commit removes the vulnerable construct entirely. The function now simply reassigns pages with 'sg_set_page(dst + j, page, plen, sg[i].offset)' without attempting to manipulate dst_offset, which prevents the off-by-one overflow condition.

bic_trace_step.reason: The af_alg_pull_tsgl function (lines 559-616) contains the vulnerable construct. The loop iterates through pages with `for (i = 0, j = 0; i < sgl->cur; i++)` and processes each page by calculating `size_t plen = min_t(size_t, used, sg[i].length)`. However, there is no bounds check to ensure that `used > 0` before attempting to reassign a page to dst. The vulnerability occurs when the loop continues even after `used` becomes 0. At line 603, `used -= plen` can result in `used` becoming 0, but the loop continues to the next iteration without checking if `used` is still positive. This allows the code to attempt page reassignment (lines 589-598) even when no data remains to be processed, causing an off-by-one overflow. The fix would require adding a check like `if (!used) break;` or `if (used == 0) return;` before or after the page processing logic to prevent processing when no bytes remain.
